ai.title: Refine continuation logging and empty file handling
ai.summary: Updated `main-prompt.ts` to log the last line of the response during continuation and return an empty string for `readFilesMessage` when `filePaths` is empty. This prevents unnecessary whitespace or prompt pollution when no files are relevant.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question that doesn't involve any code files, it no longer inserts a stray blank line or empty file prompt that used to pollute the response. The assistant also now records the exact last line it was working on before continuing a long answer, so developers can better trace where generation paused and resumed. You might notice slightly cleaner outputs when no files are relevant to your request.

ai.title: System prompt warns against writing tool calls when explaining tools
ai.summary: Added instruction to system prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts warning agents not to write out <tool_call name="..." /> unless actually intending to call the tool. Prevents accidental tool execution when explaining available tools. Internal prompt refinement only.

eli5.text: The instructions that guide the assistant were quietly tweaked so that when it describes the tools it can use, it no longer accidentally triggers one of those tools by writing out its name in a special format. The change only affects how the assistant talks internally and leaves what you actually experience unchanged.

ai.title: Trim trailing whitespace in main-prompt assistant messages
ai.summary: Applied trim() to fullResponse before constructing assistant messages in main-prompt.ts. This ensures trailing end whitespace is stripped from continuedMessages and final message payloads. Scope limited to backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Prevents whitespace artifacts in model context.

eli5.text: The assistant now cleans up invisible leftover spaces at the end of its replies before they're shown to you, so you won't see stray blank padding trailing off the last line of a continued response. This only affects follow-up assistant messages in the internal prompt flow, and it's live today.

ai.title: Add LinkedIn Insight Tag to web footer
ai.summary: Added `nextjs-linkedin-insight-tag` dependency and rendered `<LinkedInInsightTag />` in `web/src/components/footer.tsx`. Introduced optional `NEXT_PUBLIC_LINKEDIN_PARTNER_ID` in `web/src/env.mjs` for tag configuration. Scope limited to web marketing analytics integration.

eli5.text: If you visit any page on the company's website, a small piece of LinkedIn tracking code now runs in your browser that helps record visits and measure how well the website brings in interested visitors. The code uses a LinkedIn partner number that the site's operators can set quietly in the background, and the company can turn this tracking on or off just by changing that one setting. This is live on the website today for anyone who lands on any page, and it affects every visitor regardless of whether they have a LinkedIn account. If you look at a page and peek at your browser's network activity, you'll see a request going to LinkedIn's servers carrying a partner identifier whenever the website loads.

ai.title: Add LinkedIn lifatid capture to landing page
ai.summary: Home page captures `li_fat_id` query param into localStorage via `useSearchParams` and `useEffect`. New `analytics.knowledge.md` documents the multi-step conversion tracking flow for upgrades and subscription checkouts using `nextjs-linkedin-insight-tag`. Scope limited to `web/src/app/page.tsx` and docs.

eli5.text: When you land on the homepage through a LinkedIn ad, the site now quietly saves a LinkedIn tracking ID to your browser's local storage so your visit can be connected to future actions. The homepage reads the tracking ID from the URL and stores it, and a new guide documents how this ID follows your upgrade or checkout steps later using LinkedIn's tracking tag. This means LinkedIn can correctly attribute your eventual subscription to the original ad, even if you don't sign up right away.

ai.title: Add LinkedIn tracking to pricing page
ai.summary: Added `linkedInTrack` call in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` using ID 353503946 when a `li_fat_id` exists in localStorage. Updated `web/src/app/page.tsx` to remove `li_fat_id` from URL params via `window.history.replaceState` after storing it. This ensures clean URLs and consistent tracking across the home and pricing pages.

eli5.text: Visitors who arrive on the site with a special LinkedIn tracking code in their web address will now have that code saved and removed from the address bar, and the same code will be passed along when they reach the pricing page so LinkedIn can attribute signups correctly. This only affects people who click through from LinkedIn ads that include that tracking parameter; regular visitors who land directly on the site or navigate normally are unaffected.

ai.title: Pricing page LinkedIn campaign ID tracking update
ai.summary: Hardcoded LinkedIn campaign ID 353503946 replaced with constant LINKED_IN_CAMPAIGN_ID (719181716) in web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx. The new ID reflects updated campaign tracking for 'Codebuff YC'. Scope limited to pricing page conversion tracking.

eli5.text: The pricing page now sends a different tracking number to LinkedIn when someone signs up, so the company can correctly attribute traffic from its 'Codebuff YC' campaign. If you looked at the page, you wouldn't see any visible change, the switch happens behind the scenes in the code. This only affects how the team measures the success of that specific marketing effort.

ai.title: Add shared Stripe checkout and LinkedIn tracking helpers
ai.summary: Shared `handleCreateCheckoutSession` in `web/src/lib/stripe.ts` and `trackUpgradeClick` in `web/src/lib/linkedin.ts` replace inline checkout and LinkedIn code in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` and `web/src/components/navbar/user-dropdown.tsx`. The new helper reads `li_fat_id`, calls `linkedInTrack`, removes the stored value, and appends `?ref=linkedin&li_fat_id=...` to the checkout-session request before redirecting through Stripe. Scope is web pricing, navbar dropdown, and related knowledge docs; the dropdown checkout flow now uses the same tracking path as pricing.

eli5.text: When you sign up for a paid plan on the website, the system now consistently records whether you came from LinkedIn's ad tracking, whether you clicked an upgrade button in the pricing page or the account menu in the top-right corner. Before, those two places handled the tracking separately, which meant some LinkedIn referrals could be missed. Now both paths use the same shared logic to log the attribution before sending you to Stripe's secure checkout page.
